frequency_question: How often do announced major tariffs proceed to implementation on schedule rather than being delayed, rescinded, or replaced by a negotiated agreement?
membership_rule: Includes: unilateral executive tariff announcements with specific future effective dates >60 days out. Excludes: standard multi-lateral WTO dispute resolutions and routine anti-dumping administrative duties.

cases.name: US Section 301 China Tariffs (Tranche 3 announced July 2018, implemented Sept 2018)
US Steel and Aluminum Tariffs (announced March 2018, implemented March 2018)
Trump proposed Mexico Tariffs over immigration (announced May 2019, suspended June 2019)
US Section 232 Auto Tariffs threat (announced 2018, repeatedly delayed and never implemented)
Trump proposed 100% BRICS tariff threat (announced late 2024, status pending/mostly rhetorical)

coverage_note: 5 prominent modern historical precedents selected as a direct reference class for executive tariff threats used as leverage.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller minor commodity adjustments; focuses strictly on major geopolitical trade threat escalations.
skeleton: Threatened bilateral trade actions over the past 3 decades categorized by whether advance signals of negotiation led to suspension.
multiplier: 2 hits out of 5 major prominent threatened tariff showdowns with lead times = 2/5 base rate.
validity_reason: Bound to the current presidential administration's specific negotiation style and executive trade action patterns.
